rightsDescription: Top-tier SEC package formerly held by CBS (SEC on CBS, 1996-2023): first weekly football selection on ABC, ABC primetime games, the SEC Championship Game on ABC, and top men's basketball inventory. Sits on top of the separate ESPN/SEC Network agreement (sec-espn-network-2014).
escalator: Not disclosed; reported as an average of about $300M a year over 10 years.
inventory: ABC 3:30 p.m. ET 'SEC on ABC': the first SEC pick each week (the old CBS slot)
ABC primetime (Saturday Night Football) SEC games
SEC Championship Game on ABC (Atlanta); ends after the 2026 game because the 24-team CFP drops Power 4 title games from 2027
Men's basketball: ABC/ESPN top games, incl. the SEC tournament final
exclusivity: Exclusive. Together with sec-espn-network-2014 it makes ESPN/ABC the SEC's only national partner.
proRataNotes: ESPN's SEC agreements were reportedly amended pro rata when Texas and Oklahoma joined in July 2024 (one On3-cited estimate: about $21M per new school). The exact amendment is not public.
renegotiationTriggers: SEC moved to a 9-game conference schedule from 2026. Front Office Sports reported that ESPN wanted more SEC games while the SEC wanted more money; the outcome was not confirmed
Loss of the SEC Championship Game from 2027 (24-team CFP). ESPN reportedly gets back about $140M a year in Power 4 title-game rights inside the new CFP addendum
note: Announced Dec. 10, 2020 under Greg Sankey. CBS chose not to match. Front Office Sports and Awful Announcing put ESPN's all-in SEC spend at about $710M a year, and Sankey has called the deal undervalued compared with the Big Ten.

rightsDescription: 20-year ESPN–SEC agreement, announced May 2013, that created the SEC Network (launched Aug. 14, 2014) and absorbed the 2008 ESPN deal (15 years, $2.25B). Covers all SEC inventory not in the top package: ESPN/ESPN2/ESPNU, SEC Network, SEC Network+ and ESPN streaming.
escalator: Not disclosed. Includes SEC Network revenue sharing, so value moves with network carriage fees and subscribers.
inventory: ESPN/ESPN2 Saturday windows (noon, 4 p.m., 7:45 p.m. ET)
SEC Network: usually 3 football games per Saturday (noon / 4:15 / 7:45) plus most basketball and Olympic sports
SEC Network+ / ESPN streaming (ESPN Unlimited/Select): non-conference and Olympic-sport events
exclusivity: Exclusive grant of conference rights; ESPN owns and runs the SEC Network.
proRataNotes: Amended with the top-tier deal for Texas and Oklahoma (2024).
renegotiationTriggers: Network carriage renewals (e.g. the Disney–YouTube TV blackout from Oct. 30 to Nov. 14, 2025 took SEC Network off YouTube TV for two weeks)
note: The $410M a year is derived: the reported $710M a year all-in ESPN figure minus the $300M top-tier package. The split is not public. Not re-verified this session because the shared web-search budget ran out.

rightsDescription: Lead Big Ten partner: FOX noon window ('Big Noon Saturday'), FOX/FS1 football and men's basketball, the Big Ten Championship Game in most years, and the conference's BTN joint venture (see big-ten-btn-2007).
escalator: Back-loaded. A Big Ten source said the biggest increases come in Years 3–7 of the 7-year term.
inventory: FOX 'Big Noon Saturday' noon ET window: the Big Ten's top game most weeks (about 24-25 games a year across FOX and FS1)
Big Ten Championship Game: originally 4 of 7 years (2023, 2025, 2027, 2029); FOX also bought NBC's 2026 game for a reported $45-55M. The 2027 and 2029 games disappear under the 24-team CFP
FS1 football and men's basketball, incl. Big Ten tournament games
Black Friday / Thanksgiving-week games (shared rotation)
exclusivity: Exclusive national window; the networks license their inventory through BTN, which FOX controls.
proRataNotes: No automatic pro rata clause has been reported. USC and UCLA were included in the 2022 negotiation; Oregon and Washington (2024) joined on reduced, phased shares.
renegotiationTriggers: 24-team CFP from 2027 removes the Big Ten Championship Game (FOX inventory); no compensation terms reported
Deal expires after 2029-30; the next negotiation window is expected about 2027-29
Paused 'Big Ten Enterprises' private-capital plan (UC Investments, $2.4B for about 10%, grant of rights to 2046) would have bundled media and sponsorship rights
note: The $400M+ a year is a Bloomberg-reported estimate (2022); the total is derived (7 x $400M). The overall 7-year package was reported at 'more than $7 billion'.

rightsDescription: 'Big Ten on CBS' 3:30 p.m. ET Saturday window (replacing the SEC on CBS slot), plus men's basketball incl. the Big Ten tournament final, and the Big Ten Championship Game in 2 of 7 years.
inventory: CBS 3:30 p.m. ET Saturday national window (about 14-15 football games a year, incl. a Black Friday game)
Big Ten Championship Game 2024 (aired) and 2028 (removed by the 24-team CFP)
Men's basketball on CBS, incl. the tournament championship; Paramount+ simulcasts
renegotiationTriggers: Loss of the 2028 Big Ten Championship Game under the 24-team CFP
note: About $350M a year per 2022 multi-outlet reports; the total is derived.

rightsDescription: 'Big Ten Saturday Night' primetime package on NBC, Peacock-exclusive football games, and men's and women's basketball on NBC/Peacock. NBC's single Big Ten Championship Game (2026) was resold to FOX.
inventory: NBC Saturday primetime (7:30 p.m. ET) 'Big Ten Saturday Night' (about 14-16 games a year)
Peacock-exclusive football games (streaming only)
Basketball on NBC/Peacock
2026 Big Ten Championship Game sold back to FOX for a reported $45-55M (NBC had asked about $70M); NBC received extra regular-season games in return
renegotiationTriggers: April 2026 resale of the 2026 title game to FOX shows a network can sublicense or resell inventory, but FOX (through BTN's licensing role) blocked NBC from selling it to a streamer
note: About $350M a year per 2022 reports; the total is derived.

rightsDescription: Big Ten Network joint venture (launched Aug. 30, 2007): FOX majority owner (about 61%), Big Ten about 39%. BTN holds the licensing rights for the conference's media inventory and carries third-tier football, most basketball and Olympic sports. The Big Ten earns equity profits plus rights fees.
escalator: Driven by carriage fees: high in-footprint rates, low out-of-footprint rates.
inventory: BTN football: noon/3:30/primetime games not chosen by FOX/CBS/NBC
Most men's/women's basketball and Olympic sports
B1G+ subscription streaming for non-televised events
renegotiationTriggers: Expansion into new TV markets (LA, Seattle, Portland in 2024) lets BTN demand in-footprint carriage fees from distributors there
note: The ownership split and the JV term (originally 25 years, which would run to about 2032) come from prior knowledge, not re-verified this session. Search reporting does confirm that FOX holds a majority stake and that BTN holds the licensing rights for Big Ten inventory.

rightsDescription: Six-year extension, signed Oct. 2022, nearly 18 months before the exclusive window opened: ESPN/ABC share of Big 12 football and basketball, plus 'Big 12 Now on ESPN+' streaming of non-televised events.
inventory: ABC 3:30 p.m. ET and ABC primetime Big 12 games (ESPN and FOX alternate picks)
ESPN/ESPN2/ESPNU windows incl. Thursday/Friday night games
Big 12 Now on ESPN+ (streaming-only, roughly 1,000 events a year incl. some football)
Big 12 Championship Game (alternates ABC/FOX) through the 2026 season; dropped from 2027 under the 24-team CFP
Men's and women's basketball, incl. the Big 12 tournament in Kansas City
proRataNotes: Both the ESPN and FOX contracts include a pro rata clause for expansion. Adding Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah (2024) raised payments by about one average share each (about $31.7M).
renegotiationTriggers: Pro rata increases when members are added
Next cycle expected around 2029-30. A May 2026 report had Yormark already planning it, but he leaves on Jan. 31, 2027 to run RedBird Capital's Milan Sports & Entertainment
Big 12 Championship Game eliminated from 2027 (24-team CFP)
note: The package was $2.28B over 6 years (about $380M a year) for 12 members, roughly $31.7M per school. The 16-member figure (about $507M a year) is derived at $31.7M per school. The ESPN/FOX split is not public, so the per-partner value is null.

rightsDescription: FOX share of the six-year Big 12 extension: FOX/FS1 football incl. Big Noon Saturday appearances, and FS1 basketball.
inventory: FOX 'Big Noon Saturday' Big 12 games (shared with the Big Ten)
FOX/FS1 afternoon and primetime football
Big 12 Championship Game in alternating years through 2026
FS1 men's basketball
renegotiationTriggers: See big-12-espn-2025
note: Package value: see big-12-espn-2025.

rightsDescription: 20-year ESPN agreement (announced July 2016) covering all ACC rights and creating the ACC Network (launched Aug. 22, 2019), tied to a grant of rights through 2035-36. ESPN had an option, due Feb. 1, 2025, to keep the 2027-28 to 2035-36 years; it exercised the option on Jan. 30, 2025.
escalator: Not disclosed. The original 2012 deal was reported at $3.6B over 15 years (about $240M a year), and value has risen with ACC Network carriage.
inventory: ABC Saturday windows incl. ABC primetime ACC games
ESPN/ESPN2 incl. Thursday and Friday night ACC games
ACC Network: 1-3 football games most Saturdays plus most basketball and Olympic sports
ACCNX / ESPN streaming for non-televised events
ACC Championship Game (ABC, Charlotte) through the 2026 season; eliminated from 2027 under the 24-team CFP
Some games sublicensed to The CW (see acc-cw-2023)
exclusivity: Exclusive; ESPN owns and runs the ACC Network.
proRataNotes: ESPN pays pro rata for Cal, Stanford and SMU (joined 2024). Cal and Stanford took reduced shares (about 30% at first) and SMU took none for 9 years; the money they gave up funds a performance and success-initiative pool. Per-school pro rata amount reportedly about $24M (low confidence).
renegotiationTriggers: ESPN option exercised Jan. 30, 2025. Commissioner Jim Phillips called it a 'look-in' that could also cover time slots and network designations
March 2025 settlement with Florida State and Clemson: revenue distribution partly tied to viewership/brand value, and lower exit costs after 2030-31 (see the legal-exit-fees-gor research)
ACC Championship Game eliminated from 2027 (24-team CFP)
note: The extension and option facts are verified. Value is undisclosed; the game model can estimate ACC TV income at about $24-28M per school a year before the success-initiative pool.

rightsDescription: The CW sublicenses a slate of ACC football (Saturday afternoon) and men's/women's basketball games from ESPN, giving the ACC free over-the-air exposure.

ACC basketball on The CW

Outlets project the total package at $7-10M per school a year ($56-80M total for 8 football schools); $68M is the midpoint, and The Athletic's Dellenger reported the final figure would be below earlier $8-15M projections.
